items.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)?

options.rationale: Breach documentation is a separate incident activity.

options.text: To identify and mitigate privacy risks before high-risk processing begins
options.rationale: Correct: a DPIA is a forward-looking assessment that identifies and reduces privacy risk prior to high-risk processing.

options.text: To replace the organization's privacy policy
options.rationale: A DPIA does not replace policies.

options.text: To certify a product as compliant
options.rationale: A DPIA is a risk tool, not a certification.

items.explanation: Correct: a DPIA is a forward-looking assessment that identifies and reduces privacy risk prior to high-risk processing.

items.stem: Which metric best demonstrates privacy program OUTCOMES rather than mere activity?

options.text: Reduction in substantiated privacy complaints over time
options.rationale: Correct: a downward trend in substantiated complaints reflects an outcome of program effectiveness.
Publishing count is an activity measure.
Time spent is an input, not an outcome.

items.explanation: Correct: a downward trend in substantiated complaints reflects an outcome of program effectiveness.

items.stem: Which TWO elements belong in the initial framework for a privacy program? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: scope and objectives anchor the program framework.

options.text: Alignment to applicable laws and standards
options.rationale: Correct: legal and standards alignment is a core framework element.

options.text: A fixed breach-notification letter template only
options.rationale: A single template is an operational artifact, not the framework.
Vendor marketing is irrelevant to the framework.
Competitor products do not define the framework.

items.explanation: Both keyed options are correct; all-or-nothing scoring requires exactly the keyed set.
